title: Implement deterministic priority and tie breaking in signal event router
description:
Build the single ordered decision router in mike_trade/signals/router.py. Put the unit tests in tests/unit/test_router_ordering.py.

Required behavior:
- One DecisionRouter receives everything headed for decisions:
  - evaluation results from the i.2 EvaluationPool
  - CRITICAL events from the i.2 queueing layer: fills, broker order updates, reconciliation, stop/protective events, safety exits, manual close/flatten
  It emits them to one serialized consumer, the portfolio/order decision path. Exactly one consumer mutates account, portfolio or order state at a time. Use a single asyncio consumer or an asyncio.Lock, documented in code.
- Deterministic priority (highest first):
  1. fills and broker order updates
  2. reconciliation and drift events
  3. protective stop events and safety exits
  4. manual close/flatten requests
  5. SELL/exit strategy signals
  6. BUY/entry strategy signals
- Tie-breaking within the same priority is deterministic:
  1. event time UTC
  2. snapshot_version
  3. symbol
  4. strategy_id
  5. a monotonic sequence number assigned on arrival
  Identical input sets in any arrival order produce identical output order when timestamps and keys are equal. Arrival sequence is the final tie-breaker.
- Revalidation before authorization: a strategy signal is forwarded as actionable only if all of these hold, using an injected clock and a freshness provider:
  - its expiry has not passed
  - its snapshot_version is still the latest for that symbol
  - market data is fresh within the configured max age
  Otherwise it is recorded as REJECTED with a reason code (EXPIRED, SUPERSEDED or STALE_DATA) and not forwarded.
- ERROR, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED and STALE_DISCARDED results are recorded as non-actionable outcomes and are never routed as entries or exits.
- Duplicate suppression: the same (strategy_id, side, symbol, bar key) signal is forwarded at most once.
- Fills, broker updates, reconciliation, stop and safety events are never dropped, expired or rejected by freshness checks. They bypass discretionary revalidation.
- The router itself never calls brokers, sizes orders or applies risk rules. It only orders, revalidates and hands off to an injected consumer callable or port.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/scheduling/workers.py and mike_trade/scheduling/queueing.py (i.2) for result and CRITICAL event types
- mike_trade/scheduling/scheduler.py and triggers.py (i.1) for DueEvaluation keys
- mike_trade/signals/ (existing modules, if present) and mike_trade/domain/ for signal, side and expiry types
- mike_trade/market_data/context.py (h.4) for freshness and snapshot version
acceptance_criteria: A test submits a mixed batch (BUY signal, SELL signal, manual close, stop event, reconciliation event, fill) in shuffled arrival orders. The emitted order follows the documented priority in every permutation.

A test with equal priority and equal timestamps confirms tie-breaking by snapshot_version, then symbol, then strategy_id, then arrival sequence, and that repeated runs produce byte-identical ordering.

A test confirms that a signal past its expiry is rejected with reason EXPIRED, a signal whose snapshot_version is superseded is rejected with SUPERSEDED, and a signal whose data age exceeds max age is rejected with STALE_DATA. None reaches the consumer.
A test confirms ERROR, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED and STALE_DISCARDED outcomes never reach the consumer as entries or exits.
A test confirms that a fill or stop event older than any freshness threshold is still delivered to the consumer exactly once.
A test confirms a duplicate signal for the same (strategy_id, side, symbol, bar key) is forwarded at most once.
A concurrency test submits events from many concurrent producers and confirms the consumer never runs re-entrantly, using an in-consumer overlap detector that records zero overlaps.
router.py imports no broker or provider adapter and performs no sizing or risk evaluation.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
modify scheduling/scheduler.py, triggers.py, workers.py or queueing.py; adapt via their public APIs only
drop, expire or freshness-reject fills, broker updates, reconciliation, stop or safety events
route ERROR/TIMEOUT/CANCELLED/STALE_DISCARDED outcomes as BUY or SELL
call brokers, size orders or apply risk rules in the router
run broad test suites or backtests
